subject: Groundstation private cluster: preflight orchestration & storage constraints
messages:

To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@groundstation.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: GroundStation private cluster: preflight kick-off

Jordan —

Thanks for agreeing to run through the preflight for our on-prem private cluster. We want Redwood Private deployed into our Salt Lake City facility (VLAN-segmented, FIPS 140-2 KMS) and need a short checklist from you to unblock procurement and site ops. High level asks:

- Minimum cluster size you recommend for initial rollout (pods: inference + control plane, GPU mix)
- Nodepool separation and hardware profiles (ephemeral vs. blockstore requirements)
- Storage class guidance for model checkpoints / prompt cache / audit logs (encryption-at-rest + retention)
- Any network egress / firewall rules we should pre-provision (ports, NAT, private link)
- Documentation we can attach to our SOC2 evidence binder

We aim for a sprint-zero start week of Nov 8th, procurement target Nov 1st. Can you confirm if that timeline is feasible and what procurement artifacts you need? I attached our current rack layout (rack_layout_v3.pdf).

Appreciate it —
Samir
GroundStation AI — Head of Cloud Operations

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: GroundStation private cluster: preflight kick-off

Samir —

Thanks, and thanks for the rack layout. Timeline looks tight but doable with a compact scope for sprint-zero. Below is an initial checklist and a few clarifying questions so we can give procurement the right BOM and SOW.

Initial recommendations (summary):
- Minimum cluster: 3 control-plane nodes (HA), 4 worker nodes (inference), 1 small ops node (logging/metrics). If you expect heavy parallel inference, bump workers to 6.
- GPU profile: Recommend mixture of 1x A5000-equivalent / 3x A100-40GB per customer preference. We can also qualify lower-precision quantized variants if you want smaller GPUs.
- Nodepools: separate nodepools for "inference-gpu" (taints + tolerations), "stateless" (user APIs/services), and "infra" (logging/sidecars).
- Storage: two classes — fast block (local NVMe-backed PVs for model cache and KV prefix store) and encrypted network block (iSCSI/Ceph/RBD) for checkpoints and audit logs. Use a PV binding policy: RWX for shared artifacts only when necessary; prefer RWO for model checkpoints to avoid concurrency issues.
- Encryption: Redwood will integrate with your KMS (FIPS 140-2) for disk-level keys. We will need an AEAD-compatible key wrapper and a service account with limited KMS access.
- Networking: Allow inbound from our control plane endpoints (we'll provide a CIDR list) and egress to your managed observability endpoints. Block outbound internet from inference nodes except to your defined registry/proxy.

Clarifying questions:
1) Expected steady-state tokens/sec and any peak predictions for the first 3 months?
2) Do you require model artifact replication across racks (for RTO)?
3) Is there an existing HSM/KMS API we can integrate with, or will we use a vault appliance?

Procurement artifacts we need: BOM (GPU make/model, per-node RAM, local nvme capacity), rack power circuit per-rack, preferred OS image, private registry IPs, and PO contact. We'll hand you a minimal SOW (1-2 pages) and a per-node spec sheet by EOD tomorrow once you answer the three clarifiers.

Neha — copying you for the storage + PV-binding specifics (see details below).

— Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <s.desai@groundstation.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GroundStation private cluster: preflight kick-off

Samir / Jordan —

Adding storage and PV-binding guidance (operational notes):

1) PV sizing and classes:
- model-checkpoints (encrypted-net-block): RWO, default size 2TB per model (start with 3x models = 6TB), provision as thin-provisioned LVM on top of RBD/CSI. Retention policy 90 days by default (customer can extend).
- prompt-cache (local-nvme): ephemeral, use local SSD/NVMe with fast fsync; mount options noatime, DAX disabled unless your filesystem supports stable DAX semantics. We recommend ~512GB per inference node for mid-sized models; increase if you run heavy caching.
- audit-logs (archive-block): encrypted, append-only, lifecycle to object-store outside cluster nightly for long-term retention. Use retention tags for compliance.

2) Affinity/anti-affinity and failure domains:
- Use topologySpreadConstraints to spread inference pods across racks. Label nodes by rack-id (rack01/rack02) and set podAntiAffinity for critical pods.
- If you want cross-rack model replication, use async replication with a per-model RPO SLA. Cross-rack sync will add write latency; default recommendation: single-rack primary with scheduled replication windows.

3) PV binding and CSI considerations:
- Use a CSI driver that supports volume cloning and snapshotting (we recommend Rook-Ceph or Longhorn depending on site ops comfort).
- Ensure CSI has node-stage support and proper IAM mapping; Redwood will provide a reconciliation controller to reduce orphan volumes.

4) Encryption & key rotation:
- We need a KMS integration plan: key IDs, rotation cadence, and a service principal with key-encrypt-decrypt only. If you have an HSM appliance behind an API, provide endpoint and sample creds in a secure channel.

5) Backups / retention for compliance:
- Nightly snapshot to an on-site object-store + S3-replica to offsite object storage for audit logs.

Attachments: pv-binding-matrix.xlsx (simple mapping of workloads -> class -> size).

If this looks good we can paste the exact BOM items into the SOW.

-Neha
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Samir —

Thanks for the quick answers on capacity earlier today (we reviewed offline). Below is a short mutual action plan to get procurement and site ops moving:

MVP action list (target dates):
- Oct 16: GroundStation to confirm GPU make/model and rack power circuits (procurement). (owner: Procurement)
- Oct 18: Redwood sends final SOW + per-node spec sheet and network CIDR list (owner: Jordan)
- Oct 22: Site to provision VLANs and KMS test endpoint (owner: GroundStation Ops)
- Nov 1: Hardware order cutoff for Nov 8 sprint-zero start (owner: Procurement)

Canary and rollout notes: we recommend a canary consisting of 1 inference node + 1 infra node in rack01 with monitoring probes for model load, KV cache hit-rate, and disk latency. If canary meets latency and IO SLOs after 48 hours we proceed to scale to full worker set.

Next steps for me: produce a 2-page SOW and the per-node BOM today and upload to your shared drive. Neha — please attach the PV binding matrix to the SOW and include the recommended snapshot schedule in-line. Marissa / Karthik — I may need 15 minutes tomorrow to review the SOW before I send it to procurement.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this over the line.
